catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused on the CAS (Continuous Architecture System) runner, governance action engines, steering projection runtime, and multi-agent architecture pipeline.
analysis_limits: Dynamic multi-agent interactions and live LLM latency behaviors are inferred from static flow documentation, model contracts, and test specs.

system_map.overview: The CAS runner is an agentic continuous architecture platform that validates, steers, and reconciles software architecture artifacts. It coordinates agentic tasks using a centralised FlowRunner, enforcing compliance guardrails and capability lineage tracking.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Reconciles and synthesizes architectural knowledge, pull requests, and governance artifacts through LLM-assisted structured merging.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Evaluates compliance rules, executes safe lifecycle transitions for architectural artifacts, and raises governance findings.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Sequentially schedules, orchestrates, and manages context passing across multi-step agentic analysis, validation, and generation pipelines.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner executes sequential multi-step architectural pipelines, propagating execution context across governance, validation, and agentic merge steps.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access to downstream LLM inference providers with configurable retry and fallback logic.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides deterministic, offline responses for CI/CD test execution and sandbox runs.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Captures traces, latency, and operational tokens during agentic workflows.

state_and_memory.description: File-based architectural knowledge store under cas-knowledge/ containing decisions, rules, patterns, and steering templates.
Runtime execution profiles, prompt facts, and delta indexes materialized into memory during a pipeline run.
Governance health scores, compliance findings, and traceable metrics calculated dynamically from raw git and capability deltas.

patterns.name: Agentic Knowledge Reconciler

tool_protocols.notes: Uses structured LLM invocations to parse delta changes and resolve architectural conflicts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prioritizes correct resolution of conflicting architectural directives over execution speed.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomous synthesis is bounded by typed resolution models and strict schema schemas.

patterns.summary: Uses an LLM agent to analyze semantic architectural deltas and produce structured reconciliation plans rather than raw text merges.
patterns.intent: Resolve non-trivial, multi-source changes to architectural policies and patterns without introducing structural contradictions.
patterns.context: Executed during CI/CD merges when architectural artifacts or steering profiles are modified across multiple branches or projects.
forces: Standard git three-way text merging cannot resolve semantic conflicts across architectural rules.
Full human review for every minor architectural delta creates a bottleneck in autonomous development cycles.
patterns.solution: AgenticMerger inspects incoming RawGitDelta and CapabilityLineage objects, crafts structured synthesis prompts via LiteLLMClient, and maps output to a ResolutionResult model.
implementation_signals: Invocation of AgenticMerger in pipeline runner
Mapping LLM completions directly into ResolutionResult Pydantic schema
Extraction of git diffs into structured delta models before LLM evaluation

evidence.note: Defines agentic merge lifecycle and output reconciliation.
Defines the deterministic outputs required from reconciliation operations.

benefits: Semantic consistency across distributed architectural decision records.
Reduces human toil in resolving non-overlapping rule adjustments.
costs: Inference latency on pull request builds.
Token costs proportional to diff sizes.
failure_modes: Hallucination of non-existent policy precedents if delta context exceeds window.

patterns.reuse_notes: Extractable to any system managing schema-constrained documentation or policy-as-code reconciliation.

patterns.name: Finite Transition Governance Guardrail

tool_protocols.notes: Deterministic state validation executed locally prior to executing agent actions.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unauthorized or invalid architectural state jumps.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents may request lifecycle transitions, but a rigid transition registry enforces strict state transitions.

patterns.summary: Restricts autonomous agent actions to state changes explicitly validated by an authoritative transition registry.
patterns.intent: Prevent LLM or autonomous processes from promoting, deprecating, or skipping architectural artifact lifecycle states arbitrarily.
patterns.context: When a run requests a state mutation for an Architecture Decision Record (ADR), Pattern, or Rule.
forces: Autonomous agents tend to bypass intermediate states (e.g. promoting 'proposed' directly to 'retired') if unconstrained.
Hard-coding transitions across disparate agent handlers leads to security drift.
patterns.solution: GovernanceActionEngine validates proposed actions against TransitionRegistry before applying modifications to the governance inventory.
implementation_signals: Existence of TransitionRegistry class encapsulating state validity logic
GovernanceAction model containing explicit source and destination lifecycle states
Pre-condition rejection before LLM outputs are persisted

evidence.note: Restricts artifact state updates to predefined legal state edges.
Applies vetted transitions as atomic business services.

benefits: Zero illegal state transitions in persistent architectural repositories.
costs: Requires explicit definition of all valid lifecycle permutations upfront.
failure_modes: Engine raises GovernanceException and stops pipeline when an unanticipated edge case is triggered.

patterns.reuse_notes: Easily adapted to any tool-use agent framework where agent tool-calls perform database or state updates.

patterns.name: Steering Fact Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Pre-computes contextual facts into schema-compliant prompt inputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Injects only relevant capabilities into prompts, minimizing prompt bloat and token overhead.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Decouples knowledge indexing from LLM prompt construction.

patterns.summary: Compiles raw architectural repository metadata and lineage records into discrete, prompt-ready fact objects for dynamic agent context injection.
patterns.intent: Provide agents with verified ground-truth context without needing ad-hoc embeddings or uncontrolled filesystem traversal.
patterns.context: Used during pipeline initialization to project governance and steering expectations into the runtime memory of the agent.
forces: Passing raw markdown or git histories directly consumes excessive context tokens.
Unstructured context injection increases the likelihood of model hallucination regarding current architectural constraints.
patterns.solution: Transform capability records into typed PromptFact instances and organize them inside a SteeringRuntimeIndex ready for template insertion.
implementation_signals: Pydantic model PromptFact capturing key-value or assertion-like structures
SteeringRuntimeIndex aggregating capabilities and lineage facts
Workflow steps dedicated to steering projection prior to execution

evidence.note: Declares explicit fact projection models used for prompt rendering.
CI workflow executing steering projection compilation.

benefits: Deterministic prompt generation across identical commit hashes.
Reduced prompt tokens through curated fact selection.
costs: Pre-computation step required prior to invoking agent workflows.
failure_modes: Stale index if file alterations occur mid-pipeline without rebuilding the steering projection.

patterns.reuse_notes: Pattern can be reused in coding assistants where repository architecture must be injected concisely into prompts.

patterns.name: Dual-Mode LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Wraps multi-provider routing behind uniform callable interfaces.

optimisation_targets.notes: Allows running comprehensive end-to-end integration tests without live LLM API keys or costs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Hides model-specific nuances and network flakiness from high-level agentic components.

patterns.summary: Isolates model invocation behind a provider client interface pairing a multi-model gateway (LiteLLM) with a fully deterministic mock client.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent business logic from specific cloud LLM APIs and allow zero-cost deterministic offline testing.
patterns.context: Instantiated by runners, analyzers, and mergers to execute LLM inferences.
forces: Directly binding agents to a specific LLM SDK makes multi-cloud deployment or model migration arduous.
CI pipelines fail or accrue massive costs when executing integration tests against live LLMs.
patterns.solution: Implement a shared protocol or client hierarchy exposing identical completion methods implemented by LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient.
implementation_signals: Pair of client modules: litellm_client.py and mock_client.py with matching interface signatures
Configuration toggles switching between live and mock clients during runtime initialization

evidence.note: Production LLM wrapper handling API calls via LiteLLM.
Mock client delivering canned deterministic responses for test runs.

benefits: Zero API cost and zero network flakiness in automated regression suites.
Vendor neutrality and frictionless switching between OpenAI, Anthropic, or local models.
costs: Mock client fixtures must be updated when prompt contracts or expected outputs change.
failure_modes: Mock drift where mock responses pass tests but production LLM outputs fail schema parsing.

patterns.reuse_notes: Universally applicable to any agentic system needing robust testability and vendor independence.

patterns.name: Lineage-Aware Architectural Delta Slicing

tool_protocols.notes: Processes git changes into typed capability records before evaluation.

optimisation_targets.notes: Assures changes are categorized by architectural capability impact.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Structures raw changes into typed categories prior to handing control to agent reasoning.

patterns.summary: Transforms unstructured git diffs into structured capability records and lineage graphs prior to agent evaluation.
patterns.intent: Provide reasoning agents with categorized functional changes rather than raw line-by-line diffs.
patterns.context: Triggered when evaluating pull requests or branch merges against known architectural capabilities.
forces: Raw git diffs contain irrelevant syntactic changes (whitespace, imports) that distract the LLM.
Tracing how changes affect long-term system capabilities requires structured delta lineage.
patterns.solution: Parse git outputs into RawGitDelta, map modified components to CapabilityRecord and CapabilityLineage, and emit ArchitecturalDelta objects for evaluation.
implementation_signals: Models defining CapabilityCategory, CapabilityRecordType, and CapabilityLineage
ArchitecturalDelta model uniting git delta metadata with affected capabilities

evidence.note: Data models for delta and lineage decomposition.
Outlines flow from code modifications to architectural delta classification.

benefits: High signal-to-noise ratio in agent prompts.
Explicit architectural traceability back to git commit histories.
costs: Pre-processing pipeline complexity in parsing git patches.
failure_modes: Unmapped files or unknown capability types falling through delta extraction without analysis.

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable in code review bots, architectural drift detection, and compliance auditing systems.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline Orchestration

tool_protocols.notes: Steps communicate via centralized runner execution context.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures reproducible pipeline runs in automated CI environments.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Coordinates steps in strict sequence rather than emergent dynamic dispatch.

patterns.summary: Coordinates multi-step agent and deterministic evaluation tasks through a centralised, linear execution runner with shared context propagation.
patterns.intent: Execute ordered architectural analysis and synthesis steps deterministically, terminating immediately on critical compliance failures.
patterns.context: The central coordinator for executing CAS commands via CLI or GitHub Actions workflows.
forces: Autonomous agent loops can spin indefinitely or deviate without strict step boundaries.
CI/CD systems demand deterministic exit codes and structured stage results.
patterns.solution: FlowRunner coordinates pipeline execution, sequentially advancing through validation, steering projection, agentic resolution, and reporting.
implementation_signals: Central FlowRunner class orchestrating stages
Ordered invocation of validation engines, mergers, and index builders
Step execution summaries aggregated into final run report

evidence.note: Main execution engine managing workflow phases.
Visualizes sequential flow and checkpointing logic.

benefits: Predictable execution timing and deterministic behavior in automated pipelines.
costs: Cannot naturally branch into parallel exploratory agent swarms without runner refactoring.
failure_modes: Early step failure aborts subsequent independent analytical stages.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard orchestration pattern for production CI/CD integrated agent pipelines.

patterns.name: Compliance-Driven Health Scoring

tool_protocols.notes: Calculates health scores directly from findings and metric telemetry.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides continuous quantitative feedback on architectural drift.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic scoring functions evaluate agent findings without additional LLM subjectivity.

patterns.summary: Computes composite governance health ratings from agent-extracted compliance findings and traceable operational metrics.
patterns.intent: Transform disparate rule compliance violations into standardized health indicators (e.g., Healthy, Degraded, Critical).
patterns.context: Evaluated after rule verification steps and exposed to dashboards and workflow gates.
forces: Individual rule violations vary wildly in severity, making binary pass/fail gates too blunt.
Engineers and autonomous agents need actionable diagnostic reasons when a health rating drops.
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine generates ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics, which are ingested by calculate_health to compute GovernanceHealth and reason strings.
implementation_signals: HealthStatus enum (HEALTHY, WARNING, CRITICAL)
calculate_health and get_health_reasons functions aggregating findings into state
GovernanceHealth model encapsulating composite score

evidence.note: Scans workspace artifacts against defined compliance rules.
Computes health score enum and human-readable diagnostic reasons.
Typed models holding evaluation findings and computed metrics.

benefits: Quantifiable signal for agent feedback loops (e.g. agent can retry until health is Healthy).
costs: Scoring weights must be tuned to avoid false-positive alert fatigue.
failure_modes: Missing finding types causing health score calculation to silently omit critical regressions.

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be adapted as an evaluation harness or stopping condition in any autonomous coding agent workflow.

patterns.name: File-Backed Blackboard Workspace

tool_protocols.notes: Agents read and mutate workspace knowledge files directly on the filesystem.

optimisation_targets.notes: Leverages Git as an immutable, auditable persistence layer for agent state.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Eliminates external database dependencies by storing shared agent memory directly in version-controlled markdown and json files.

patterns.summary: Uses a standardised, version-controlled filesystem structure as a shared blackboard for agent memory, templates, and runtime context.
patterns.intent: Allow multiple independent scripts, agents, and CI workflows to share, persist, and version state without requiring an external database.
patterns.context: Initialized during bootstrap (bootstrap.py) and referenced by all runtime evaluation steps.
forces: External state stores (Redis, PostgreSQL) add infrastructure overhead and cannot easily be checked out at specific git revisions.
Agent steps need shared access to global rules, templates, and runtime execution contexts.
patterns.solution: Bootstrap initializes standard directory hierarchies (cas-knowledge/global, cas-knowledge/runtime, cas-knowledge/projects) and populates rule-context.json and execution-profile.yaml.
implementation_signals: Workspace initialization logic in bootstrap.py creating structured directories
merge_cas_governance_block embedding governance state directly into markdown/config files
cas-knowledge folder containing templates, rules, and runtime files

evidence.note: Scaffolds file hierarchy and merges governance blocks.
Blackboard runtime profile read and written by agent steps.

benefits: Complete architectural auditability: every state change is a git commit.
costs: File I/O overhead on large repositories.
Potential git merge conflicts on concurrent multi-agent branches.
failure_modes: Partial writes or corrupted JSON/YAML files leave blackboard in an unparseable state.

patterns.reuse_notes: Ideal pattern for CLI-based and GitOps-driven AI agents where auditability and branch compatibility are critical.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Raw Git Diff Dumping
symptoms: Dumping full repository diffs directly into LLM prompts without filtering or capability mapping.
Exceeding LLM context limits or causing attention dispersion on minor stylistic changes.

where_observed.note: Addressed by introducing CapabilityRecord slicing rather than passing raw diff strings directly.

impact: Increased inference costs, slower completion times, and hallucinated policy infractions on benign whitespace edits.
suggested_remediation: Slice and tokenize git diffs into typed capability records before passing them to the agent prompt context.

anti_patterns.name: Unguarded State Jump
symptoms: Accepting LLM-generated state field updates (e.g. promoting a draft to active) without validating allowed transitions.
Bypassing required peer review or validation gates.

where_observed.note: Engine explicitly guards against this by throwing GovernanceException on invalid transitions.

impact: Corrupted lifecycle statuses across architectural decisions and policy drift.
suggested_remediation: Enforce transition registry checks at the service layer prior to committing any agent action.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Prompts are rendered using strictly typed Pydantic models (PromptFact, SteeringRuntimeIndex) and validated against output schemas before downstream consumption.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Ensures prompt inputs and outputs have verifiable structural integrity.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Evaluation is carried out by ComplianceEngine and health_model.py, converting observed findings into deterministic health metrics.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Evaluation does not rely solely on LLM self-grading; deterministic algorithms score rule compliance.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: State transitions are restricted by TransitionRegistry, blocking illegal lifecycle mutations from autonomous agents.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Hard boundaries on what agents are allowed to mutate in the architecture knowledge base.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent agentic merges coordinated when multiple PRs execute AgenticMerger simultaneously?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Simultaneous merges could lead to git race conditions or conflicting resolution decisions.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Repository relies on GitHub Actions workflow serialization, but code-level file locking was not observed.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine GitHub Actions concurrency settings in .github/workflows/cas-continuous-architecture.yml.

open_questions.question: Does LiteLLMClient support automated multi-step tool call recursion or is tool-calling handled externally by FlowRunner?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether agent autonomy includes dynamic tool call loops or is constrained to single-shot completions per step.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Full step invocation loop details inside FlowRunner were partially observed in symbols.
